items.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995
items.q: The transcript shows Michael Woods is the interviewer. The interviewee (Frank Foster or Bill Hughes) does not mention any personal or professional relationship with Michael Woods outside of this interview context.

ctx.x: Bill Hughes has been a familiar face in the Basie trombone section for many years. Born in Dallas, Texas, his first band experience was with Andy Kirk. He recorded with Frank Wess in 1952, then joined Basie for the first time in 1954, staying until ‘57. His recorded solo on “Magic” is a trademark and since 1964, Bill has been a presence with the Basie Orchestra, currently holding down the bass trombone chair.
Bill and Frank were interviewed together following a concert in Schenectady, New York on March 28, 1995, by Michael Woods and Monk Rowe.

We are filming some interviews with some of the United States of America’s greatest jazz artists for Hamilton College. We are very privileged to have two members of the Count Basie Orchestra with us today. We have Frank Foster and Bill Hughes. My name is Mike Woods and I am a professor at Hamilton College, and my colleague, Monk Rowe, teaches saxophone also at the college. I’d like to start and ask you guys some questions about the Basie band and how it got started. Tell us how the Basie band kind of evolved out…
